from_notes: Fortunately for Iltutmish, Chengiz Khan returned home without entering India.
x: Chengiz Khan only reached the Indus (1221) chasing Mangbarni and turned back without crossing it. Tair Bahadur, Abdullah and Qutlugh Khwaja led raids into India.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.55; PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.31

from_notes: during the third invasion, the Mongol commander, Khwaja, advanced up to Delhi ... Zafar Khan was killed
x: The third Mongol invasion of Alauddin's reign (Kili, 1299, under Qutlugh Khwaja) killed Zafar Khan ('Jafar Khan'). Nusrat Khan fell at Ranthambore; Akat Khan was executed for rebellion.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.36-37

from_notes: In 1303, Alauddin stormed the Chittor fort. Raja Ratan Singh ... The Rajput women, including Rani Padmini, performed jauhar.
x: In Jayasi's Padmavat (1540), Padmini was the wife of Rana Ratan Singh of Chittor, whom Alauddin defeated in 1303.

from_notes: Padmavat | Malik Muhammad Jayasi | 1540, Awadhi
x: Jayasi wrote Padmavat (1540) in Awadhi, an early form of Hindi, so II is accepted; Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' (1719-48) is credited in books as the first Mughal to patronise Urdu, so I is accepted too.
source: app notes 1:106 (sub 6); CDS 2009 key

from_notes: Ghazi Malik assumed the title Ghiyas-ud-din Tughluq in A.D. 1320, marking the end of the Khilji dynasty.
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.63
x: Ghazi Malik, Alauddin's general and governor of the Punjab, killed Khusrau Khan in 1320 and founded the Tughlaq dynasty as Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.63-64

from_notes: As the salary fixed by Alauddin to the soldiers was low, controlling the market was necessary.
x: Alauddin's large standing army was paid low fixed cash salaries, so he fixed prices of daily goods so that soldiers could live comfortably on low pay. Farmers' returns and direct purchase were not the aim.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.39; NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61

from_notes: As the salary fixed by Alauddin to the soldiers was low, controlling the market was necessary.
x: Price control was meant for the soldiers of the large standing army, who were paid low fixed salaries.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.39

from_notes: He aimed to maintain a large army, leading to the lowering and fixing of prices for daily commodities.
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61
x: Alauddin did introduce price control in Delhi (A true), but to maintain a large army on low pay, not to pay lower wages to palace artisans (R false).
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61

from_notes: The government ensured a supply of grain by maintaining stocks in government storehouses.
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.62
x: Alauddin Khalji's fixed prices, state granaries and rationing are called the first 'Public Distribution System' of medieval India.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.62; app notes 1:107 (sub 8)

from_notes: Alauddin implemented a four-point plan to control prices of daily commodities.
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.62
x: Market control and rationing were Alauddin Khalji's system, set up to support his large army; Balban, Jalaluddin and the Tughluqs had no such system.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.62

x: Controlled grazing is regulating the grazing time and consumption level of a pasture to keep it productive; rotational grazing (moving stock between paddocks) is one method of it. Off-subject: environment.
source: PMF Environment 06 (controlled grazing); standard definition (FAO grazing management)

from_notes: Measurement limited to Delhi and nearby areas, not the whole empire.
x: I is true – Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure cultivated land. III is accepted in the key – he took revenue under direct state control and curbed the governors' (muqtis') independent powers. II is false – measurement was limited to Delhi and the Doab.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61; PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.40; app notes 1:107 (sub 2)

from_notes: Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan of Delhi to initiate the measurement of land.
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61
x: Masahat means measurement of land; Alauddin was the first Sultan to assess revenue on it (unit: biswa). Kismat-i-Ghalla and Ghalla-Bakhshi are crop-sharing; Ghazi is a title.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61

from_notes: He centralized administration and even confiscated religious endowments and free lands (Inam and Wakt)
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61
x: Alauddin reclaimed milk, inam and waqf grants and brought much land under khalisa (crown land) to pay his army in cash.
source: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.61; app notes 1:107 (sub 2)

x: On 21 January 2017 Bihar formed a human chain of about 11,000 km, joined by crores of people, in support of liquor prohibition. Off-subject: current affairs.

from_notes: Nobles were forbidden to hold social gatherings or festivities or to form marriage alliances without the permission of the sultan.
x: Alauddin forbade nobles to hold social gatherings and festivities or to make marriage alliances without his permission, to stop conspiracies.
source: PMF Ancient & Medieval 04 p.39

from_notes: His control over the market was highly successful, earning him the title of a "great political economist."
from_notes_src: NextGen Indian History - APPSC Exams 03 p.62
x: The sources and the keys call Alauddin's market control highly successful: prices stayed fixed even in famine and the army was kept on low pay.
